## Summary

- **Case-insensitive parsing** was already in place (field names normalized via `.lower()`); confirmed it accepts `Q:`, `q:`, `TOPIC:`, `Topic:`, etc. uniformly
- **`--validate` flag** added to `parse_items.py`: checks each item block for unknown field names and missing required `Q:`/`A:` fields, prints errors with approximate line numbers to stderr, and exits non-zero when issues are found
- **Format spec** in `items.md` expanded to clearly document required fields (`Q`, `A`), optional fields (`Topic`, `Ref`, `Date`, `Note`), and the case-insensitivity rule

## Test plan

- [ ] `python3 parse_items.py --validate` prints `OK` on the current valid `items.md`
- [ ] A file missing `A:` on an item reports `item missing required field 'A:'` and exits 1
- [ ] A file with an unknown field (e.g. `Foo:`) reports `unknown field 'Foo:'` and exits 1
- [ ] Mixed-case field names (`TOPIC:`, `q:`) still parse correctly

Closes #5

> Dual-agent review by **Claude** and **Codex**.

## Summary of PR/Issue

PR #6 closes issue #5 by adding a `--validate` CLI flag to `parse_items.py` that checks each item block for unknown or missing required fields, printing errors with approximate line numbers and exiting non-zero on failure. It also expands the format spec header in `items.md` to document required vs. optional fields and the case-insensitivity rule. The PR correctly notes that case-insensitive field parsing was already delivered by PR #4 and does not re-implement it. Changes are lean: +38 lines to `parse_items.py`, +15/-3 lines to `items.md`.

## Review

The implementation is well-scoped and correct in its core logic, but the new `validate_items()` function has two concrete correctness gaps that result in false-OK results for malformed input. Neither causes data loss, but they undermine the stated purpose of the feature.

| Issue | Severity | Description |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Duplicate fields silently pass | WARNING | `fields` tracks occurrence counts but never checks `> 1`; a block with two `A:` lines gets `fields["a"] = 2` and passes all checks |
| Empty required fields silently pass | WARNING | `A:` with no value matches the regex with an empty group 2; the field is counted as present, so the required-field check passes |
| No automated tests | INFO | Test plan is entirely manual; the project has no regression safety net as logic accumulates across parse/validate/quiz/export |
| `validate_items()` duplicates parse logic | INFO | Re-reads the file independently using a string `.split()` instead of `re.split()`; divergence risk if the separator rule ever changes in `parse_items()` |
| `--validate` help text omits exit code contract | INFO | `"Check file for format errors and exit"` does not tell scripters that exit 0 means clean and exit 1 means errors |

## Progress

- Case-insensitive field parsing was already implemented in PR #4; the PR correctly identifies this and does not re-implement it.
- The `items.md` format spec block is clear, accurate, and fully addresses what issue #5 asked for.
- The rubrics reviewer confirmed no active rubrics are configured for this repo; no rubric-gated gaps apply.

## Issue Details

<details>
<summary>Duplicate fields silently pass</summary>

**Cause:** `fields[key] = fields.get(key, 0) + 1` accumulates a count per field name, but the only checks downstream are `if fields:` (non-empty) and `if field not in fields` (presence). A count of 2 for `"a"` is treated identically to a count of 1.

**Candidate solutions:**
- After incrementing, check `if fields[key] > 1: errors.append(f"line ~{start_line}: duplicate field '{key.upper()}:'")`.
- Alternatively, switch `fields` from `dict[str, int]` to a `set[str]` and emit the duplicate-field error at the point of collision; this removes the dead counting code entirely.

**Comments:** The inline comment at [`parse_items.py` line 52](https://github.com/bnewm0609/learning-tools-sepo/pull/6#discussion_r3329543816) covers this.

</details>

<details>
<summary>Empty required fields silently pass</summary>

**Cause:** `re.match(r"^([A-Za-z]+):\s*(.*)", "A:")` matches with `m.group(2) == ""`. The field is recorded in `fields`, so `if "a" not in fields` evaluates to `False` and no error is emitted. The downstream parser also records `item["a"] = ""`, which is structurally valid but almost certainly a data-entry mistake.

**Candidate solutions:**
- After extracting `key`, check `if not m.group(2).strip(): errors.append(f"line ~{start_line}: required field '{key.upper()}:' has no value")` for fields in `REQUIRED_FIELDS`.
- Or check the stripped value at the point of the required-field loop: `if fields.get(field, 0) == 0 or not (value tracked separately)...` — though this requires also tracking values, making the first approach cleaner.

</details>

<details>
<summary>No automated tests</summary>

**Cause:** No test infrastructure exists in the repository yet.

**Candidate solutions:** Add a minimal `pytest` suite with three cases: a valid file returns `[]`, a file missing `A:` returns one error, a file with an unknown field returns one error. This is not blocking today, but the project is accumulating untested logic.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`validate_items()` duplicates parse logic</summary>

**Cause:** Both functions read the file and tokenize by `"\n---\n"`, but `parse_items()` uses `re.split(r"\n---\n", text)` while `validate_items()` uses `text.split("\n---\n")`. These are functionally identical but will diverge if someone loosens the separator regex in `parse_items()` (e.g., to tolerate trailing whitespace on `---` lines).

**Candidate solutions:** For a project this size, extracting a shared `_split_blocks(text)` helper is sufficient. Alternatively, refactor `validate_items()` to call `parse_items()` for fields it can derive, and only add validator-specific checks on top.

</details>

<details>
<summary>`--validate` help text omits exit code contract</summary>

**Cause:** Current: `"Check file for format errors and exit"`. The exit-code behavior (0 = OK, 1 = errors) is a scripting contract that should be visible in `--help`.

**Candidate solutions:** Change to `"Validate format; exits 0 on success, 1 on errors"`.

</details>

## Progress

- Posted one inline comment on [`parse_items.py` line 52](https://github.com/bnewm0609/learning-tools-sepo/pull/6#discussion_r3329543816) covering the duplicate-field dead-code WARNING.

## Recommended Next Step

`FIX_PR`: Both WARNINGs are concrete, localized, and safe for an automated fix — each is a small addition to `validate_items()` with no interface changes.

## Final Verdict

`MINOR_ISSUES`

## Action Items

- [ ] `parse_items.py` `validate_items()`: check `fields[key] > 1` after incrementing and emit a "duplicate field" error, or switch `fields` to a `set` to remove the dead counting
- [ ] `parse_items.py` `validate_items()`: check that required-field values are non-empty (e.g. `A:` with no text should be an error)
- [ ] `parse_items.py` `--validate` help string: document exit-code semantics (`exits 0 on success, 1 on errors`)
